entry.title: A clearer view of the power ahead
entry.summary: The IEA’s updated outlook puts global data-center electricity consumption at roughly 950 TWh in 2030, from 485 TWh in 2025. Grid delivery and equipment supply remain important to realizing that growth.

entry.title: A longer horizon for firm power
entry.summary: DOE describes a 400 GW U.S. nuclear capacity goal for 2050. It is an economy-wide ambition; tracking operational additions will help distinguish the target from delivered power.

entry.title: An advanced manufacturing milestone
entry.summary: TSMC reports that its 2 nm technology entered high-volume manufacturing in the fourth quarter of 2025. Its annual report also describes expanding manufacturing capacity across regions.

entry.title: Another chapter in Wisconsin’s buildout
entry.summary: Microsoft announced an additional $4 billion commitment for a second Wisconsin data center over three years. The pledge is tracked separately from completed construction and actual expenditure.

entry.title: Useful model capability became more affordable
entry.summary: Stanford’s 2025 AI Index records a drop from $20 to $0.07 per million tokens at a GPT-3.5-equivalent benchmark threshold between November 2022 and October 2024.

entry.title: AI reaches more organizations
entry.summary: The 2026 AI Index reports organizational AI adoption of 88%, following 78% in the previous report. These survey results track use; measured business outcomes remain a separate research question.

entry.title: Veo 3 zero-shot video reasoning
entry.summary: Google DeepMind’s Veo 3 demonstrated zero-shot abilities to simulate physical behaviors like buoyancy and maze solving across more than 18,000 generated videos, indicating emergent video reasoning without task-specific training.
